# Meteo Product Chain

How the thirteen meteo product notebooks
([`10_METEO/30_PRODUCTS`](notebooks/index.html)) turn screened measurements into
the finished variables, and which of them depend on each other.

The numbering is a run order: a notebook reads only products whose number is
lower than its own, so running `01` to `13` and then the merge `99` satisfies
every dependency. Only four of those reads change an exported value: `02` and
`03` take `01`'s gap-filled `SW_IN` as a gap-fill driver, and `07` computes
`VPD` from `02` and `04`. All the others are diagnostic — `06` reads `01` and
`02`; `08` reads `02`, `05` and `06`; `09` reads `02` and `08`; `10` reads `02`
and `09`; `11` reads `09` and `10`; `12` reads `01`; `13` reads `02` and `06`. A
diagnostic read changes what a notebook concludes, not what it writes.

Six products have no external reference at all, which the diagram makes visible.
No weather service measures this plot's soil, and nothing anywhere near the site
measures the radiation this canopy sends back. `09` (`SWC`), `10` (`TS`) and
`11` (`G`) are therefore checked against the other depths and plates of their
own profile, and `06` (`LW_IN`), `12` (`SW_OUT`) and `13` (`LW_OUT`) against the
other channel of the same radiometer and against physics.

## Reading the diagram

**Blue products are gap-filled or reference-filled** (`SW_IN`, `TA`, `PPFD_IN`,
`PREC`, `TS`), **green products ship as measured** (`RH`, `PA`, `LW_IN`, `SWC`,
`G`, `SW_OUT`, `LW_OUT`), and the **orange product is computed** from other
products (`VPD`).

A few things the edges make explicit:

- **Two notebooks do not read the database.** `07` downloads nothing at all: it
  reads two finished product files and applies a formula. `10` reads the database
  indirectly, through the screened `TS` files that
  `TS_FF1_SCREENED_30MIN_2004-2025` downloads once, so that the 34 channels are
  not re-queried every time a decision in `10` is revisited. `09` reads the early
  half of that same download, as its witness for the June 2015 wiring break.
- **`01` is the hub of the chain.** Its gap-filled `SW_IN_T1_47_1_gfXG` is a
  driver in both the `TA` and the `PPFD_IN` gap-fill models, which is why the
  order `01` → `02` / `03` is real and not just a naming convention. It is also
  the diagnostic partner of the two notebooks that describe the other channels of
  the same radiometer, `06` and `12`.
- **`02` is read by more notebooks than any other product**, by six of them, and
  in only one does it change a value. Air temperature separates rain from snow in
  `08`, excludes snowmelt in `09`, and gives the Stefan-Boltzmann yardstick in
  `06` and `13`; the arrow into `07` is the one that writes. Every notebook that
  reads it across January 2016 reads the `HOMOGENIZED` column, because the
  measured one carries the acquisition step of that date.
- **`08` (`PREC`) reads more references than any other notebook** — three files,
  for two different jobs. The Ehrendingen (`OED`) record arrives as two products,
  daily up to September 2014 and 30MIN after, and the 30MIN half is what fills
  the gaps. The regional ensemble is a different tool: one nearby gauge can show
  *that* the tower changed in 2018, but only a dozen of them can show *which
  side* of that break is wrong, which is what the homogenisation factors rest on.
  `09` reads that same ensemble, for a third job again: its jump detector must not
  read a gap in the tower gauge as a dry spell.
- **`05` reads the MeteoSwiss pressure as a diagnostic only** (dashed): it checks
  the tower record but never writes a value into it. The NABEL hut barometer it
  also downloads is likewise diagnostic and is not exported.
- **Where there is no external reference, a second channel takes its place.**
  `09` (`SWC`), `10` (`TS`) and `11` (`G`) are checked against the other depths
  and plates of their own profile. `06` (`LW_IN`) and `13` (`LW_OUT`) are checked
  against the Stefan-Boltzmann emission at `02`'s air temperature, and `13`
  additionally against `06`, the second pyrgeometer of the same instrument. `12`
  (`SW_OUT`) is checked against `01`, because `SW_OUT / SW_IN` is the surface
  albedo and anything that scales both channels of one radiometer together
  cancels in that ratio. None of these reads writes a value: they catch a
  whole-record error such as a wrong file, a wrong unit or a shifted year, but
  cannot validate any single measurement.

## What `99` merges

Notebook `99` concatenates the value and flag columns of the individual products
into one half-hourly table and re-checks the joined index. Its `PRODUCTS` list
covers `01`–`13`: 29 data series and, beside them, 30 flag columns, 59 in all.
`10` and `11` contribute only their reconciled series — seven soil-temperature
depths and one soil heat flux — because a merged column is one variable or one
depth, whereas the 18 soil-temperature channels and the three plates are one
sensor each. Those stay in their own product files.

`TA`, `PREC` and four of the five `SWC` depths enter the merge **twice**, because
each exports two value columns: the measured series and the homogenised one.
Each is listed as two entries so that both get their own overview figure, and the
loader skips a column it has already taken, so a shared file cannot be merged in
twice.

Only six of the 29 series cover the whole period; the rest may legitimately
contain `NaN`. `05` (`PA`), `06` (`LW_IN`), `12` (`SW_OUT`) and `13` (`LW_OUT`)
export as measured and their sensors start in September 2005; the soil series of
`09`, `10` and `11` begin in September 2004, or in April 2020 for the depths the
2020 profile added, and they lose the forest-floor logger outages; `PREC` keeps
the 2,224 half-hours before September 2014 that have no
sub-daily reference to fill them from. The merge check carries a reason for each
and asserts completeness for everything else.

Precipitation aggregates differently from the other products: **rainfall sums,
it does not average**. Every entry in `PRODUCTS` therefore names its
aggregation. A daily mean of 30-minute rainfall is approximately 0.05 mm and is
not an interpretable quantity, whereas the daily total is.
